title: Captain Summit — Strategy and Guardrails
summary: Weekly leadership all-hands focused on aligning Q4 priorities: reliability SLAs, Dedicated and Private rollout guardrails, hiring tempo adjustments, and a new incident playbook. Leadership emphasized cost/performance levers and a phased hiring plan; several action items assigned for next sprint.
action_items: Maya: Draft Q4 Dedicated rollout guardrails doc and share by 2027-11-04
Owen: Run megabatch perf run on v2-runtime, attach latency tail graphs by 2027-11-02
Priya: Publish hiring cadence update and interview rubric by 2027-11-01
Luis: Propose cost-savings targets for infra (3rd party licensing and batch configs) by 2027-11-07
next_steps: Leadership to review guardrails doc in Slack channel #captain-summit
All teams to submit top two risks for Q4 by end of week
Townhall follow-up email with links to benchmarks and security pack
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-28
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 1:12
Attendees: Avery, Jordan, Owen, Maya, Luis, Priya, Samira + company-wide dial-in

Summary (auto): Leadership review of operational guardrails for Dedicated and Private, hiring cadence adjustments to match revenue momentum, incident response and reliability targets.

[00:00] Avery (CEO): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know this is a packed week — quick housekeeping: recording is on, notes will be posted. We're here for the captain summit — short and pragmatic. I'll kick off with the topline numbers for the month.
[00:22] Jordan (CPO): Hey all — revenue is tracking +18% quarter-on-quarter, usage uptick on embedding endpoints; latencies are ok on avg but tails creeping up on long-seq requests.
[00:40] Maya (Head of Platform): yep, we saw tail events last Friday — looks like a KV cache eviction pattern plus a weird scheduling jitter on the v2 runtime under burst. We're investigating.
[00:58] Luis (VP Eng): and to add, the Dedicated pools that had the custom kernel landed saw a 12% perf improvement but higher mem fragmentation, so we need the kernel/alloc revisit.
[01:20] Avery: OK, that's the concrete background. Today I want three things: one, agree on guardrails for Dedicated and Private rollouts so sales can commit; two, calibrate hiring cadence given the financials; three, lock in an incident playbook for reliability. Short updates and then open Q&A.

[02:00] Maya: I'll lead the guardrails conversation. Draft principles: "predictable throughput, regional parity, controlled feature set for GA, and clear rollback policies". The tricky bit is how opinionated we should be on kernel sets — if we force a narrow kernel matrix we reduce variability but slow model onboarding.
[02:28] Owen: we should differentiate runtime variants: a "conservative" runtime for Private with strict kernel pins and a "fast path" for Hosted where we can tune aggressively. The private customers with air-gapped requirements will accept a more conservative surface.
[02:50] Jordan: Sales wants a yes/no on whether we can promise 99.9 p99 latency for Dedicated. We can't promise that until we add prefix caching for long chat sessions and a better autoscaler.
[03:12] Maya: Agree. Suggest a three-tier SLA: Bronze (best-effort), Silver (99.5 p99), Gold (99.9 p99) where Gold requires minimum reserved capacity and specific batching configs. That also maps to pricing.
[03:40] Luis: Implementation detail: Gold would require static allocation and a saturation monitor. That imposes cost. We need to make sure customers understand the economics.
[04:00] Priya (Head of People): quick HR note — if we're leaning into more Gold commitments we need to staff SRE layers and on-call rotation adjustments. Hiring ask incoming.

[04:36] Samira (GM EMEA): From EMEA perspective customers care about data residency and KMS options. Private + VPC is table stakes for a number of RFPs right now. If Guardrails outline KMS/HSM integration timelines that helps.
[04:58] Avery: Good. Put KMS timelines in the guardrails.

[05:18] Jordan: Switching to hiring — revenue growth justifies headcount but not a full-scale ramp. Priya, can we do a controlled hire plan: focus on SRE, Platform, and a small growth ops pod?
[05:36] Priya: Yes. Proposal: freeze non-critical IC hiring for 4 weeks, prioritize critical SRE and Platform roles; open two senior SRE requisitions and one principal infra PM this quarter. We'll publish rubrics.
[05:56] Avery: That sounds reasonable. Also, we'll accelerate contractor-to-hire conversions where screen + ramp is minimal.

[06:18] Owen: Back to runtime — I ran a sanity megabatch on the v2-runtime on Monday, the 99th percentile climbed when sequence lengths exceeded 4k tokens; KV cache thrash plus tensor-copy overheads. There were also some ops-level scheduling race logs that look intermittent.
[06:42] Maya: do you think quantization profile or a different kernel selection would help? Sometimes the quantized path is faster but adds tail variance.
[06:58] Owen: For acute tail reductions we should consider a bounded-batch policy for long sequences and separate smaller-worker lanes. Long sequences shouldn't sit with short low-latency requests.

[07:20] Jordan: That's a good operational control — a lane separation policy. Could be part of the guardrails doc too.

[07:36] [Audience murmurs / clapping emoji in chat]

[08:00] Luis: Cost notes — if we ship lane separation we might double cross-lane unused capacity. We need a cost model to show unit economics for Gold SLAs. I'll own a first-pass model.
[08:20] Maya: Also, caching TTLs and prefix caching for chat will recover tokens; we should add prefix/KV caching guidelines. Note: transcription sometimes shows K-V cash in ops notes, haha.
[08:36] Riley (Engineer on the call, misattributed as Speaker 8): yeah, I saw K-V cash in the logs — it's a typo.

[09:00] Avery: small pivot: incident playbook. We had a recent SLO breach and the postmortem highlighted three gaps: unclear on escalation, no customer-facing template, and missing runbook ownership. We need a single document.
[09:20] Owen: propose a one-page incident playbook that maps severity to response, who declares SEV, customer comm cadence, and a triage checklist. Also a template for the customer-facing postmortem.
[09:44] Priya: link to hiring — we need a rotational SEV lead and to backfill on-call to avoid burn.

[10:00] Maya: Draft of the incident playbook will be in the engineering wiki. I'll make a first draft and share.

[10:18] Avery: Great. Let's do a quick Q&A. Please keep questions brief.

[10:28] Speaker 3 (Engineering lead): question on Dedicated GA timing — are we aiming for early Q1 or late Q4? Sales wants to put early Q1 in proposals.
[10:44] Jordan: sales can say "private beta in Q4, GA early Q1" — but include the caveat about guardrails and required reserved capacity for Gold.

[11:00] Speaker 4 (Product): any change to the model catalog policy? Customers want more open-model options but that increases kernel testing.
[11:16] Owen: we'll gate new models with a compatibility matrix. New models go to canary, then a performance gate after X production hours. That reduces surprise.

[11:36] Speaker 5 (Support): request for a standard security FAQ to answer common SOC2 and ISO questions in proposals.
[11:50] Samira: good call — I think the security pack needs to be a single artifact we can hand to sales; security will own that with support from Compliance.

[12:04] Avery: ok last block — culture and people. Priya?
[12:12] Priya: quick update on comp cycles: compensation refresh will happen in Q1, not before. We will publish calibration timelines for managers; for now, hiring rubrics and interview guides will be posted. Also, reminder about the caregiver policy update that goes live next month.
[12:36] Avery: thanks. One ask — every leader, in the next 72 hours, put two prioritized risks for Q4 into the #captain-summit channel. We'll use this to shape the guardrails.

[12:54] Jordan: to close, we want clarity: guardrails doc (Maya), incident playbook (Owen/Maya), hiring cadence doc (Priya) and a cost model (Luis). We'll reconvene in two weeks with drafts.

[13:18] Audience: rapid-fire questions in chat — a couple about private deployment pricing and KMS timeline, will cover in doc.

[13:40] Avery: Thanks everyone. Quick reminders: townhall recording + slides posted, and we have the all-hands offsite RSVP open. Meeting adjourned.
